$comment: THE SAME TEST, FOR ALL SIX LANGUAGES. Drift ships six SDKs so a customer can
build in the language their team already uses, and that promise is worth
exactly as much as the weakest one. Six independently-worded test suites can
each pass while asserting subtly different things — which is how Go came to
round-trip a local blob correctly while the other five silently did not.
So the assertions live HERE, once, and each language ships a thin driver that
performs the operations and prints what it got. check.py compares the two.
A language cannot quietly hold a weaker opinion about what correct means.
Every case runs against the LOCAL store — no BACKBONE_URL, no running slice —
because that is the loop a developer meets first and the one where the six
drifted apart. The edge cases call a loopback peer each driver stands up, which
echoes the path it was asked for and the X-Drift-Slice header it received.

blob_with_bucket.why: Put then Get must return the bytes. The failure shape being guarded against is a Put that reports success and a Get that returns empty with no error — indistinguishable from 'I stored an empty value'.

blob_without_bucket.why: A bare name has no bucket, so it lands in the default one and must come back from there rather than from whatever the slash-splitting produced.

blob_absent.why: THE CONTROL, and the sharpest case here. A key that was never written must FAIL — Go answers a 404 — and the driver reports the string "error" when the call raises. An SDK that returns empty-with-no-error instead reports null and fails this case, which is exactly the defect the two cases above cannot catch on their own: an implementation that returns empty for EVERYTHING passes both of them by accident.

list_in_order.why: ListInOrder exists solely to fix the order a plain List returns. Twelve documents, inserted 1..12, must come back 1..12.

list_default_order.why: THE CONTROL for the one above, and the contract a paging caller already holds. The DEFAULT read is byte order over the storage key, which for twelve documents is 1,10,11,12,2,…,9 — documented behaviour, not a bug. Adding the ordered variant must not change it.

list_all_in_order_count.why: ListAllInOrder pages, so the ordered cursor has to advance in the ordered sequence rather than in key order. 1200 documents crosses the 1000-row page cap, which is where a cursor that advances by key silently truncates.

list_all_in_order_first.why: The first document of the first page.

list_all_in_order_boundary.why: The document either side of the page boundary is where a wrong cursor loses or repeats rows.

list_all_in_order_last.why: The last document of the last page.

list_filter_two_fields.why: A filter with two entries returns the documents matching BOTH, as a slice does. Of x1 (a=1,b=1), x2 (a=1,b=2), x3 (a=2,b=1) and x4 (a=3,b=2), only x2 has a=1 AND b=2. An SDK honouring one entry answers two documents — the first entry's pair or the last's — and a handler acting on that touches records it never asked for.

list_filter_one_field.why: THE CONTROL for the one above. A single entry reads exactly as it always has: a=1 is x1 and x2. Without it, an SDK that returned x2 for every filter would pass the case above.

list_filter_over_cap.why: A slice refuses a filter of more than 8 entries with a 400, so a local run refuses it too. The document matches all nine entries, so an SDK that applies no cap answers it rather than failing. Rust's list has no error channel and reads any refusal as no rows, the same way it reads a slice's 400; its driver reports that as the error.

edge_slice_url.why: Edge.Slice(name) reaches the slice a link names. The driver links `billing-api` by setting DRIFT_LINK_BILLING_API_URL to a loopback peer under /base/, calls GET /api/events, and reports the path the peer saw. The name's dash becomes an underscore in the variable, and the base path is kept, so a wrong variable or a dropped base both show here.

slice_url.why: THE CONTROL for the one above, and the alias contract: the deprecated Slice(name) spelling must keep working and reach the same link. An SDK whose Edge spelling read a different variable would pass one of these two and fail the other.

edge_slice_not_linked.why: A slice with no link refuses before any network I/O, and the refusal names where a link is declared: edge.links in the Driftfile, with the CLI command beside it. The text is the same in all six languages so a developer reads one message whichever SDK they use.
edge_slice_not_linked.expect: drift: slice "billing" is not linked: declare it under edge.links in the Driftfile (or run drift slice link add billing)

slice_not_linked.why: The deprecated spelling refuses with the same message, because it is the same client.
slice_not_linked.expect: drift: slice "billing" is not linked: declare it under edge.links in the Driftfile (or run drift slice link add billing)

slice_identity_absent.why: With no DRIFT_SLICE in the environment, which is the normal case for a function, the call carries NO X-Drift-Slice header. An empty header asserts an identity of "" rather than none, and reads as a real answer to anything checking for presence. The peer reports null when the header is absent.

slice_identity_kept.why: With DRIFT_SLICE=billing, a caller passing its own X-Drift-Slice: operator must not relabel the call. The header is a label and authorises nothing either way, but an SDK that lets the caller's copy win, or sends both, hands code a documented way to pose as another slice.
